title: Test Coverage
concept: Test coverage measures which parts of your code are exercised by tests — guiding you to untested edge cases and contract paths.
why: You can't improve what you don't measure. Coverage reports reveal blind spots: functions never called, branches never taken, contracts never checked.
theory:
## Understanding Coverage

### Types of Coverage

| Type | What it measures |
|------|-----------------|
| Line coverage | Which lines executed |
| Branch coverage | Which if/else branches taken |
| Contract coverage | Which requires/ensures checked |
| Function coverage | Which functions called |

### Running Coverage
```sh
# Run tests with coverage
xiom test --coverage

# Generate coverage report
xiom coverage report

# Open HTML report
xiom coverage open
```

### Coverage Output
```
=== Coverage Summary ===
Lines:      85.2% (231/271)
Branches:   72.1% (62/86)
Contracts:  90.0% (18/20)
Functions:  95.5% (21/22)

Uncovered:
  src/parser.xi:45   fn parse_error_recovery
  src/parser.xi:89   if branch: EOF handling
  src/math.xi:23     requires: n >= 0 (unchecked)
```

### What to Test

1. **Every function** — at minimum, one test per function
2. **Every contract path** — test requires violations AND satisfactions
3. **Every error variant** — test each way a function can fail
4. **Edge cases** — empty, max, min, zero, negative
5. **Boundaries** — values just inside and just outside valid ranges

### Contract Coverage Specifically
```xiom
fn divide(a: Int, b: Int) -> Int
  requires: b != 0;

// Test 1: satisfies contract (b != 0)
assert_eq(divide(10, 2), 5);

// Test 2: violates contract (ensure caller handles it)
// This tests the CALLER's error handling, not the function
```
syntax_ref:
# Run coverage:
xiom test --coverage
xiom coverage report

# Target: 80%+ line coverage
# Critical: 100% contract coverage
tips: Aim for 80%+ line coverage and 100% contract coverage
Uncovered code IS a risk — either test it or document why it's unreachable
Coverage is necessary but not sufficient — 100% coverage doesn't mean 100% correct
Focus on branch coverage — it catches untested logic paths that line coverage misses
common_mistakes: Chasing 100% line coverage at the expense of meaningful tests
Writing tests that execute code but don't assert anything useful
Ignoring uncovered contract branches — a contract you never test is a contract you don't trust
